name: Summit West
label: Summit West
about_prose: Summit West is one of thirteen neighborhood districts the City of Bend formally recognizes, and it is the youngest of them. The district sits in the northwest corner of the city, running from River West along Shevlin Park Road out to the edge of Deschutes National Forest land, where the paved street grid stops and gravel Forest Service roads pick up. It covers 1,553 acres across 48 subdivisions, from Northwest Quad, the smallest, to NorthWest Crossing, the largest. Downtown Bend is about 10 minutes away by car via Mt. Washington Drive to Newport Avenue. Inside the district, Bend Park and Recreation District counts 64 acres of neighborhood parks and 15 miles of trail, and both numbers roughly double once Shevlin Park is added in.

Two of the core neighborhoods trace back to the same family's land, sold off a generation apart. In 1999, the Tennant Family Limited Partnership and Brooks Resources Corporation bought roughly 487 acres from the Miller family and built NorthWest Crossing, selling the first lots by lottery in 2001 and finishing the first homes in 2002. Fifteen years later, a separate piece of Miller land, bought by Bill Miller in 1955 from a sheep rancher who had owned it since the 1920s, became The Tree Farm: 533 acres split into fifty two-acre homesites wrapped around more than 400 acres of preserved forest. In August 2017, Brooks Resources transferred 328 of those preserved acres to Bend Park and Recreation District, folding them into Shevlin Park.

The neighborhoods read differently on the ground. NorthWest Crossing was built as a walkable, new-urbanist grid, and its Architectural Review Committee holds new construction to Craftsman, Prairie, Tudor Revival, American Foursquare, and Colonial Revival forms drawn from Bend houses built between 1910 and 1930. Its town center adds 32 acres of parks plus the restaurants and shops that give the district a commercial core most Bend neighborhoods do not have inside their own street grid. The Tree Farm sits at the other end of the spectrum, with two-acre clustered lots built around forest instead of sidewalks. Shevlin Commons, a smaller 76-acre subdivision of 103 homes about four miles from downtown, splits the difference. Roughly 43 of its acres sit under a permanent conservation easement bordering the park.

What draws people to Summit West is largely what sits outside the door. Shevlin Park, donated to the city in 1920 with the deed transferred that January of 1921 and expanded through Bend Park and Recreation District land purchases beginning in 1977, backs directly onto the district. It offers a 6-mile loop through old-growth ponderosa, a 2.5-mile Tumalo Creek Trail, and a connection into the Deschutes National Forest's Mrazek Trail. About three miles up Skyliners Road, Phil's Trailhead feeds a mountain-biking network that runs to hundreds of miles of singletrack across the national forest, popular enough that its recently expanded parking lot still fills on weekends. Closer in, Discovery Park's fenced dog park, 51-bed community garden, and 3-acre irrigation lake sit inside NorthWest Crossing itself, and the 24-acre Skyline Sports Complex adds four lighted athletic fields and a seasonal disc golf course.

Schools run through Bend-La Pine district-wide. Summit High School, which lends the district its name, sits at 2855 NW Clearwater Drive. Pacific Crest Middle School is at 3030 NW Elwood Lane, and High Lakes Elementary is at 2500 NW High Lakes Loop, inside the district.

The same forest edge that gives Summit West its trail access also puts it in the wildland-urban interface, and that risk is documented, not hypothetical. On August 4, 1990, an arson fire started inside Shevlin Park, crossed the Deschutes River, and burned 3,350 acres in about ten hours, destroying 22 homes and forcing roughly 3,000 people to evacuate. Central Oregon LandWatch and local fire officials still point to that fire when they argue for buffer zones between the national forest and new construction on Bend's west side. Living against the forest here means the forest is also part of what you are managing, not just what you are looking at.

amenities.name: Shevlin Park
amenities.description: A 981-acre Bend Park and Recreation park at 18920 NW Shevlin Park Road, donated in 1920, with a 6-mile loop through old-growth ponderosa, a 2.5-mile Tumalo Creek trail, and a connection to the Deschutes National Forest Mrazek Trail.

amenities.name: Discovery Park
amenities.description: A 40-acre community park at 1315 NW Discovery Park Drive in NorthWest Crossing, with a natural play area, fenced off-leash dog park, a 51-bed community garden, and a 3-acre irrigation lake.

amenities.name: Skyline Sports Complex
amenities.description: A 24.4-acre athletic facility at 19617 Mountaineer Way, with four lighted fields, outdoor basketball courts, a playground, and a seasonal disc golf course.

amenities.name: Summit High School
amenities.description: Bend-La Pine Schools' west-side comprehensive high school at 2855 NW Clearwater Drive (grades 9-12), which gives the district its name.

amenities.name: Phil's Trail System
amenities.description: A trailhead at the district's edge connecting riders and runners to the Deschutes National Forest trail network, including the 34-mile Twin Bridges loop, an Oregon Scenic Bikeway.
amenities.access: Free; trailhead off NW Skyline Ranch Road
